newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says to cope with forex based on G7 accord.
newsitem.headline: MOF says to cope with forex based on G7 accord.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday that Japan will cope with foreign exchange movements based on an agreement among the Group of Seven (G7) nations.

"We agreed at the G7 meeting in Berlin (in February) that we will watch currency movements and cooperate as necessary. Based on this stance we will watch the market correctly," he told a news conference.

Mitsuzuka said the ministry's stance remained unchanged from before, that an excessively weak yen, as well as an excessively strong yen, was not favourable, and that it would deal appropriately with such movements.

Asked whether the current level of the yen against the dollar and the speed with which the yen had been falling could be taken as excessive, Mitsuzuka said: "At this moment I would like to refrain from making a comment concerning this."

Asked about Japan's interest rate policy, Mitsuzuka said he had merely reported the Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor's comments at a meeting of economic ministers on Tuesday, that the central bank would like to continue basing its monetary policy on strengthening the basis for Japan's economic recovery.
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita had said then that the BOJ had no intention of changing that stance, Mitsuzuka said.
